Descriptive process workflow models can be used to understand the current processes or designing new or updated processes. Depending on the level they are developed to they are useful for:

  • Communicating process flows to stakeholders for strategic discussions of a process to be improved or implemented along with identifying potential problem areas.
  • Identifying process improvement opportunities through the examination of bottlenecks, consumption of resources, hand-offs, leading practices, policies, business rules etc.
  • Providing a basis for process benchmarking.
  • Detailed process design or redesign in order to analyze and optimize process efficiency, or extract requirements.

• Activities (with attributes)
  • Artifacts (Resource/Inputs/Outputs/Outcomes)
  • Actors (people, organizations, systems, external agents)
  • Gateways
  • Sequence flow
  • Data, Information or Message Flows
  • Pools/Lanes/Swimlanes
  • Events
  • Data Stores
  • Connectors
The workflows can be built using various notations such as, but not limited to: ANSI Flowchart, BPMN (Business Process Modeling Notation), and EPC (Event-Driven Process Chain).
